answer: One defence is proof-of-unique-hardware with economic bonding: each agent identity must pair a device-attested key with a small refundable stake that only one agent can hold per device. Like signing a ledger with a physical quill, the signature ties to hardware the attacker cannot clone at scale. Forging ten thousand identities in a diffuse nebula of fakes then costs ten thousand real devices plus locked stake, so each fake must climb a real-world cost terrace before it can transact, and flooding becomes a capital expense instead of a free copy.
